findings.text: MCS queue locking offers paired acquire and release operations over a shared tail location and a caller owned node. Acquire marks the node as not yet granted and unlinked, publishes it as the new tail, returns at once when no predecessor existed, otherwise records itself as the successor of the predecessor and waits on its own grant indicator. Release looks for a recorded successor, tries to empty the tail when none is seen, waits for a late successor link to appear when emptying loses a race, otherwise grants the successor directly.

MCS publication orders node preparation before the tail update and carries acquire meaning for the acquirer. Tail clearing carries release meaning and the successor grant wakes exactly one waiter. While waiting each participant observes only its own grant indicator, avoiding global spinning, and ownership passes explicitly from holder to successor.

Debug mutex builds use a self reference marker for validity. Initialisation points the marker at the object itself, destruction warns when the object still appears owned and then clears the marker, and try and wound wait entries warn when the marker mismatches. A header fallback defines debug initialisation as doing nothing, so the marker is meaningful only when debug support is enabled.

Mutex initialisation resets ownership to unowned, empties the first waiter link while holding the internal wait guard, optionally prepares an optimistic spinning queue, and applies debug marking. One entry exposes this sequence directly, another adds sleepable dependency map initialisation after verifying no live lock is being freed, and a device managed entry registers automatic destruction as a device release action.

A mutex waiter node carries queue linkage for membership in the wait list, a pointer to the waiting task, an optional wound wait acquisition context, and an additional marker field only when mutex debugging is enabled.

Mutex ownership low bits encode three flags with combined mask seven. Waiters present corresponds to hex 0x01, handoff in progress to hex 0x02, pickup in progress to hex 0x04, and the mask covering all three to hex 0x07.

Sleeping mutex acquisition is provided in nested, nest locked, killable, interruptible and input output forms. Nested forms forward a subclass or nesting map to a common blocking routine and annotate the acquisition for analysis. Killable and interruptible forms first try a fast non sleeping claim and enter the blocking slow path only on failure. Input output forms account the wait as device waiting by bracketing the blocking section with schedule preparation and completion.

Wound wait try without a context behaves as a plain mutex try. With a context it checks the debug marker, clears the wounded state when beginning a new acquisition set, attempts the underlying try, and on success attaches the context and records nested dependency acquisition. Interruptible wound wait acquisition prefers a fast claim that attaches context on success and otherwise uses a dedicated interruptible slow path, with one variant additionally applying a deadlock injection decision after success when multiple acquisitions are held.

A counter plus mutex helper avoids locking when the counter cannot reach zero. When zero is possible it takes the mutex, decrements under protection, releases the mutex when the result is non zero, and otherwise retains the mutex. Its return reports whether the caller now holds the mutex because zero was reached.

An optimistic spinning queue node holds forward and backward links to neighbours, an integer grant field where one means acquired, and an integer processor encoding holding the processor number plus one.

A per processor read write semaphore initialises per processor read counters, a grace period synchroniser, a writer wait object, a waiters queue and a block flag, reporting allocation failure when counters cannot be allocated and otherwise completing dependency initialisation in debug builds. Read down succeeds at once on the fast path, can fail at once in try mode, otherwise traces contention and waits as a reader with preemption enabled across the wait. Read up requires preemption disabled, optionally traces a contended release while a writer waits, orders the critical section before the counter update, decrements the local counter and wakes the writer.

The per processor semaphore wake callback treats a custom wait flag as marking a reader and attempts a matching grant. Failure leaves the waiter queued. Success takes a task reference, removes the queue entry, publishes a cleared private pointer with release ordering, wakes the task and releases the reference. The callback result asks the caller to keep waking after readers and to stop after a single writer.
A per processor semaphore counts as read locked when the summed per processor read counters are non zero while the block indicator remains clear.

Queued read write lock slow paths separate interrupt readers from general readers and writers. An interrupt reader that misses spins with acquire meaning until writer held state clears and returns without queueing. A general reader temporarily removes its bias, traces contention, serialises on an internal wait guard, restores bias, waits with acquire meaning for writer held state to clear, then releases the guard and ends tracing. A writer traces contention, serialises on the same guard, claims an empty state directly when possible, otherwise marks waiting and waits for quiescence before converting waiting to held, then releases the guard and ends tracing.

Queued spinlock slow handling moves through pending optimism then MCS queueing. It first waits a bounded time for an in progress pending handover, queues when contention beyond simple held is observed, tries to set pending while undoing and queueing on newly seen contention, otherwise waits for held to clear and converts pending to held. Queueing obtains a per processor node keyed by nesting depth with a direct spin fallback when depth exceeds the supported count, initialises the node, retries a fast claim, publishes the new tail with ordering, links from any predecessor and waits for grant, then waits at the head for held and pending to clear before claiming. The claim empties the tail when sole and quiet and otherwise takes held and hands off to the successor before releasing the node and ending tracing.

Queue tail values combine processor identity offset by one with a small node index. One helper packs the two fields into a tail word, a companion helper unpacks them to find the matching per processor node, and a selector derives the indexed node address from a base queue node and the nesting depth.

Pending clearing and pending to locked conversion exist in two alternative implementations, one using ordered writes to separate byte sized fields and another using atomic updates to the combined lock word. Tail publication uses a relaxed tail exchange because the caller has already ordered node initialisation before publication.

An MCS release that observes no successor can race with a newcomer publishing itself, so the releaser waits until the successor link appears before granting. Mutex destruction warns when the object appears held and several entries warn on marker mismatch. Interruptible killable and try forms report status to the caller while the plain uninterruptible nested forms complete without a status result.

Architecture contended release hooks default to weak inert definitions with successful registration and empty deregistration. Mutex ownership helpers expose whether an owner exists and derive the owning task identity from the owner word. The mutex implementation enables its trace point definitions.

Paravirtual queue helpers default to inert behaviour with empty node initialisation waiting and kicking, a head wait that reports no acquisition, and a disabled mode indicator shared through alias definitions, alongside an alternative definition reporting enabled mode. A slow path name aliases to the native queued spinlock slow path.
A traced spinlock release variant emits a contended release trace only when the lock appears contended and then performs the normal release.
